# Sunrise Alarm

A full-screen night screen for a TV: loops [this nature video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M-2eAiU09qg) overnight, silent, at whatever brightness you set. When sunrise starts, it switches to [this sunrise video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ERlvvvNUeas), turns its sound on, and increases the volume as the screen brightens. At alarm time, it also plays [the selected alarm track](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MQm_1cteY3o) and enlarges the clock.

## How to use

1. Open the page in Chrome or Edge on a computer with internet (needed for YouTube).
2. Set your alarm time and overnight brightness (full brightness to all the way off). You can still move the brightness slider after overnight starts.
3. Choose **Start overnight**.
4. Put the browser in full screen on the TV.
5. Turn off the TV’s sleep / auto-off timer so it stays on all night.

**Preview sunrise** runs a 30-second version of the fade so you can see the light and quiet sound without waiting until morning.

## TV tips

- HDMI from a laptop or mini PC is the most reliable way to keep a file playing all night.
- On a smart TV browser, pick the video from USB or downloads if the TV allows file access.
- Keep the TV awake in its settings. The page also asks the browser not to sleep the screen when that API is available.
- Use the TV remote’s back/exit or the on-screen **Stop** / **Turn off alarm** buttons to end it.
